result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): A lists all ten signals in their original order with the exact meanings, and gives a short self-test note: cover the Meaning column and recall each one. Its summary boxes at the bottom repeat the meanings, which slightly weakens the cover-and-recall test. B changes the order to group the signals and puts a memory-cue column right next to Meaning, so covering Meaning still leaves the answers visible. B also adds invented procedures and flow rules, such as confirming a unit is back in service before assigning it and relaying hazards to every unit. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): B lists all ten signals in their original order with the exact meanings and gives a short instruction to cover the Meaning column, which suits drilling. However, its summary boxes repeat shortened meanings, so the answers can still be seen while testing. A uses the exact meanings but puts a memory-cue column right next to them that gives the answers away when the Meaning column is covered, and it adds invented 'quick reference rules' that move away from plain recall.
